subject: BrightApp onboarding: SDK migration plan, cutover & retry patterns

- A mutual action plan (dates and owners) we can attach to our internal JIRA
- SDK quickstart and minimal code samples for Node + Python
- Recommended retry/backoff and timeout values for our traffic profile (avg payload 1–2k tokens, bursts up to 150 req/s)
- Guidance on graceful endpoint migration (how to switch from our current provider to Redwood without UX errors)
- Any rate-limit handling and canarying suggestions

Can you share a one-page checklist + a short runbook that CSM/DevOps can follow?

I looped in Elena (ops) who will own the cutover on our side.

Samir — great to hear. Attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that maps owners and a recommended two-week cutover sprint. Highlights below; MAP attached as: MAP_BrightApp_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 34KB).

Quick plan (high level)
- Week 0: Tech review + sandbox access for BrightApp engineers (credentials + API keys) — owner: Rafael
- Week 1: SDK integration & smoke tests (Node + Python) — owner: BrightApp dev lead (Elena) with Redwood eng support
- Week 2: Canary & traffic shift (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with rollback gates — owners: Vanessa (Redwood) & Elena (BrightApp)

SDK quickstart (essentials)
1) Install the Redwood SDK for Node / Python
2) Use short-lived API keys (rotate in sandbox)
3) Start with test endpoint + streaming responses for UX validation

Recommended timeouts & retry pattern (starting recommendation)
- Connection timeout: 2s
- Request timeout (overall): 15s for generation endpoints, 10s for embeddings
- Retry on 429, 502, 503 with exponential backoff + jitter, max 4 retries
- Backoff schedule example: base=250ms, multiplier=2, jitter=±100ms -> 250ms, 500ms, 1s, 2s

Rate-limit handling
- If your client receives 429: honor Retry-After header when present; otherwise apply backoff and queue small bursts client-side (token-bucket 200ms refill recommended)
- Use application-level token caching for repeated prefixes to reduce tokens per call

Graceful endpoint migration (pattern)
- Dual-write model for 48 hours: send requests to Redwood and current provider; compare responses in a low-traffic canary to validate parity (hashing + automated checks)
- Start with internal API / staging users; increase traffic in gated increments with automatic rollback on quality regression or error spikes

Sample Node snippet (minimal):
```js
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
(async () => {
  try {
    const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1-base', prompt: 'Summarize this…' , timeout: 15000 });
    console.log(res.text);
  } catch (err) {
    // retry logic handled by client wrapper (see docs)
    console.error('generation failed', err);
  }
})();
```

Where possible we prefer you use the Redwood client wrappers that do automatic retry+backoff and handle Retry-After.

I'll add a more detailed runbook and a short troubleshooting matrix (errors and steps) in the follow-up.

— Rafael

Subject: Internal: Implementation checklist & monitoring hooks (cc: BrightApp)

Looping in a couple operational points we want to be explicit about for the cutover:

Implementation checklist (detailed)
- API key creation + least-privilege roles (CSM to confirm)
- Sandbox traffic warm-up: 48 hours with synthetic traffic that mirrors 75% of peak tokens
- Integrate telemetry: per-request latency, token usage, error class (429/504/5xx) + traces into your APM
- Set up alerting thresholds: 10% increase in 5xx or >10m 429s in 15 minutes = immediate pause
- Canary rollback gate: quality delta check during each traffic ramp (automated acceptance tests)

Retry template (recommended client-side)
- Errors to retry: HTTP 429, 502, 503, timeouts (ETIMEDOUT)
- Max retries: 4
- Circuit-breaker: open after 20 failures in 1 minute; half-open test after 60s

Rate shaping suggestion (for BrightApp burst profile)
- Start canary at 5–10% traffic for 2 hours, monitor token consumption and latency. If stable, move to 25% for 4 hours, then 50% for 6 hours, then 100% overnight.
- Use client token-bucket with capacity = 2x average burst (for BrightApp approx 300 tokens) and refill rate tuned to steady-state throughput.

OBSERVABILITY HOOKS (must-haves)
- request_id header propagated from client through Redwood, returned in logs
- token_count and model_version labeled in traces
- sample failed payloads (redacted PII) to a secured bucket for incident triage

I can run the acceptance tests with your eng team next week. Vanessa will own the rollout schedule on our side.

— Monica

Samir — quick delivery of the two items you asked for below. Happy to jump on a 30m run-through Tue AM.

1) Endpoint migration pattern (client-side toggle + compare) - Push a feature flag (FF) to your service that enables "redwood_comparison_mode". When enabled: duplicate outgoing requests to Redwood and to your legacy provider; do not fail the request if Redwood differs — run a lightweight similarity check and log discrepancies off-band. Pseudocode: 
```
if (featureFlag('redwood_comparison_mode')) {
  Promise.all([
    legacyProvider.request(req),
    redwoodClient.request(req)
  ]).then(([legacy, redwood]) => {
    const score = similarityHash(legacy.text, redwood.text);
    logComparison({score, reqId: req.id});
    if (score < 0.8 && alertsEnabled) alertOps();
  });
} else {
  // normal path, switch to Redwood when canary gates pass
  return redwoodClient.request(req);
}
```
2) KV / prefix caching notes (chat-heavy workloads)
- Cache stable system prompts and shared context server-side (Redis/Memcached) keyed by conversation id + truncated token hash.
- Use LRU with TTL tuned to average session length (recommend 5–30m depending on use).
- Beware cache invalidation when you change system prompts or model versions — include model_version in the cache key.

Troubleshooting matrix (short)
- 429 (rate limit): honor Retry-After; reduce client burst, increase token-bucket refill interval.
- 504 / timeout: check network egress and request-size; consider raising request timeout to 20s temporarily for long generations and apply retries with backoff.
- 403 (auth): check key scopes and rotation window; confirm clocks if using signed tokens.

Sample CURL to test a canary call:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-base","prompt":"Hello"}'
```

We'll attach a slightly longer runbook and the acceptance-test harness as a follow-up link in Drive. If Tuesday works, I'll set up a shared channel and invite Elena + your engs.
